cohort: 112 infants participating in the Microbiome Utrecht Infant Study (MUIS)
finding: While oral microbiota development was not directly associated with susceptibility to RTI development, an influx of oral taxa into the nasopharynx before and during RTIs was observed, accompanied by reduced niche differentiation, suggesting loss of ecological topography precedes RTIs.
mod_finding: Oral microbiota was driven by feeding type, followed by age, mode of delivery, and season of sampling.
